From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-05T09:01:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden latency & 503 spike on /v1/generate — diagnostics + proposed mitigations

Quick diagnostic notes from runtime traces and node-level telemetry:
- Observed pattern: frequent small GPU allocations followed by rapid evictions on our long-context execution path. Memory free lists show repeated fragmentation events (hot-slab fragmentation) that mimic GC-like behavior, causing short-duration allocation failures and upstream request retries.
- KV cache thrashing coincident with these events increases per-request latency due to cache misses and regenerating prefixes.
- Error-classified 503s correlate with short-lived allocation failures in the LLAMA-attn execution kernel on a small subset (~12%) of nodes serving the us-west pool.

Immediate mitigations (we’ve started these at 09:00 PT):
1) Enabled model fallback: route traffic for /v1/generate to the quantized-128 variant for requests >2048 tokens. This reduces per-request peak memory by ~30%.
2) Throttled long-context path: added a soft reject at 4096 tokens for high-throughput customers and client-side backpressure hints.
3) Warmed up two additional instances per affected node group and disabled aggressive KV prefetch for the hot path to avoid preloading high-cardinality prefixes.

Planned short patch (ETA ~ 90m):
- Runtime memory reclamation change (hotfix): introduce periodic coalescing of free slabs and a modest reduction in per-request preallocated buffers. This is low-risk and limited to the us-west pool. We’ll run a canary on 3 nodes first.

I’ll post an incident playbook update and share the exact node IDs and request IDs for your traces.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
